question: State the difference between a permanent magnet and an induced magnet.
mark_scheme: A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field at all times (1); an induced magnet only becomes magnetic when placed in an external magnetic field and loses its magnetism when removed (1).

question: Describe the magnetic field pattern around a bar magnet.
mark_scheme: Field lines go from north to south pole outside the magnet (1); lines are closer together near the poles where the field is strongest (1).

question: Explain three ways to increase the strength of an electromagnet.
mark_scheme: Increase the current through the coil (1); increase the number of turns of wire on the coil (1); add an iron core inside the solenoid (1).

question: Describe how Fleming's left-hand rule is used to determine the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor.
mark_scheme: Hold the left hand with thumb, index finger, and middle finger at right angles to each other (1); index finger = magnetic field direction, middle finger = conventional current direction, thumb = direction of force/motion (1).

question: A wire of length 0.5 m carries a current of 3 A in a magnetic field of flux density 0.4 T. Calculate the force on the wire.
Explain how a simple AC generator produces an alternating current.
mark_scheme: A coil of wire rotates inside a magnetic field (1); as the coil rotates, the magnetic flux through it changes, inducing a potential difference (1); the direction of the induced current reverses every half turn, producing alternating current (1).

question: Explain why a transformer only works with alternating current and not direct current.
mark_scheme: A transformer requires a changing magnetic field to induce a voltage in the secondary coil (1); DC produces a constant (non-changing) magnetic field so no voltage is induced (1).

question: A transformer has 200 turns on the primary coil and 50 turns on the secondary coil. The input voltage is 240 V. Calculate the output voltage and state what type of transformer this is.
mark_scheme: Vp/Vs = np/ns → 240/Vs = 200/50 (1); Vs = 240 × 50/200 = 60 V (1); this is a step-down transformer (1).

question: Explain why electricity is transmitted at high voltage through the National Grid.
mark_scheme: High voltage means low current for the same power (P = IV) (1); lower current reduces power loss as heat in the cables (P = I²R) (1).

question: Describe how an electric motor works.
mark_scheme: A current-carrying coil is placed in a magnetic field and experiences a force due to the motor effect (1); the split-ring commutator reverses the current every half turn so the coil continues to rotate in the same direction (1).

question: Explain four ways to increase the induced potential difference in a generator.
mark_scheme: Any three from: increase the speed of rotation of the coil (1); increase the strength of the magnetic field (1); increase the number of turns on the coil (1); increase the area of the coil (1).

question: State what is meant by the Earth's magnetic field and explain how a compass uses it.
mark_scheme: The Earth produces a magnetic field, behaving like a giant bar magnet (1); a compass needle is a small magnet that aligns with the Earth's field, pointing towards magnetic north (1).

question: Explain how an electromagnet works and describe two uses of electromagnets in everyday devices. Explain why an electromagnet is more useful than a permanent magnet in these applications.
mark_scheme: Current flows through a solenoid, creating a magnetic field; iron core becomes an induced magnet amplifying the field (1); use 1: electric bell / relay / scrapyard crane / circuit breaker (1); use 2: different device from above (1); electromagnets can be switched on and off / strength can be varied — permanent magnets cannot be switched off (1).

question: Explain the motor effect and describe how it is used in an electric motor to produce continuous rotation.
mark_scheme: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force perpendicular to both field and current (motor effect) (1); in a motor, a coil carrying current in a magnetic field experiences forces on opposite sides in opposite directions, creating a turning effect (1); the split-ring commutator reverses the current direction every half turn (1); this ensures the forces always act in the same rotational direction, producing continuous rotation (1).

question: Explain the process of electromagnetic induction and describe how it is used in a generator to produce electricity. Include the factors that affect the size of the induced potential difference.
mark_scheme: Electromagnetic induction: a changing magnetic field through a conductor induces a potential difference (1); in a generator, a coil rotates in a magnetic field — flux through the coil changes continuously (1); this induces an alternating potential difference / alternating current (1); induced PD increases with: faster rotation / stronger magnetic field / more turns on coil / larger coil area (1 for any two factors); if the coil is connected to an external circuit, an induced current flows (1).

question: Explain how a transformer works and why transformers are essential to the operation of the National Grid. Include a calculation in your answer.
mark_scheme: AC in primary coil creates a changing magnetic field in the iron core (1); changing field induces a potential difference in the secondary coil (1); step-up transformers increase voltage for transmission — reduces current (1); lower current means less power lost as heat in cables: P = I²R (1); step-down transformers reduce voltage to safe levels for homes (1). Calculation: correct use of Vp/Vs = np/ns with own values, correctly solved (1). [Max 5]

question: Compare permanent magnets and electromagnets. In your answer, discuss their properties, how their magnetic fields are produced, and evaluate which is more suitable for use in a scrapyard crane and in a compass.
mark_scheme: Permanent magnet: always magnetic, field cannot be switched off, made from hard magnetic material like steel (1); electromagnet: magnetic only when current flows, field can be switched on/off, strength can be varied (1); scrapyard crane: electromagnet is better — can be switched off to release metal objects (1); compass: permanent magnet is better — needs to work without a power supply / always points north reliably (1); well-reasoned comparison with reference to both applications (1).

question: Evaluate the role of the National Grid in distributing electricity efficiently across the country. In your answer, explain why high voltage is used for transmission, the role of transformers, and discuss any disadvantages of the current system.
mark_scheme: National Grid transmits electricity from power stations to consumers via cables and transformers (1); step-up transformers increase voltage before transmission, reducing current (1); lower current reduces power loss in cables: P = I²R — less energy wasted as heat (1); step-down transformers reduce voltage to safe levels (230 V) for homes (1); disadvantage: high-voltage cables are a safety hazard / pylons are visually unappealing / energy is still lost despite high voltage (1); well-reasoned conclusion about overall efficiency and importance of the National Grid (1).

question: Evaluate the use of electric motors compared to combustion engines for powering vehicles. In your answer, explain how an electric motor works and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each power source, including environmental considerations.
mark_scheme: Electric motor: current-carrying coil in magnetic field experiences a force — motor effect — producing rotation (1); split-ring commutator ensures continuous rotation in one direction (1); advantage of electric motor: no direct emissions / quieter / more energy efficient / lower running costs (1); disadvantage: depends on battery range / charging infrastructure / battery production has environmental impact (1); combustion engine: burns fuel releasing CO₂ and pollutants / contributes to climate change (1); well-reasoned conclusion considering environmental and practical factors (1).
